items.title: Princeton University Press Partners with Cashmere on AI Licensing
items.excerpt: Princeton University Press has partnered with Cashmere, an AI content-licensing platform, to make its academic catalog available to 'copyright-compliant' AI tools focused on retrieval-augmented generation. Shows scholarly publishers building sanctioned licensing pipelines for AI training/RAG instead of only fighting scraping — a concrete shift in how publishers monetize and control their catalogs for AI.

items.title: More Typos, Fewer Em Dashes: Writers Are Creating an Anti-AI 'Literary Counterculture'
items.excerpt: Novelists, journalists and essayists are deliberately introducing typos, sentence fragments and fewer em-dashes to avoid sounding like a chatbot, forming an anti-AI 'literary counterculture'; some literary magazines now add 'no AI polish' notes to submission guidelines. A craft-level shift in how prose signals human authorship. (Date verified via Lit Hub Daily Jul 30 2026 roundup + Nieman Lab; wired.com is crawler-blocked for direct fetch.)

items.title: Illustrators, Authors and Musicians Are Winning Their AI Lawsuits
items.excerpt: A run of favorable rulings and settlements for illustrators, authors and musicians in AI copyright suits against Google, Meta and Anthropic is reshaping the rights landscape creators (including book authors) depend on. (Date sourced from Lit Hub Daily Jul 30 2026 roundup, which links this as that day's news; theverge.com is crawler-blocked for direct fetch — curator should treat the date as high-confidence but not article-extracted.)

items.title: ‘Genius’ Novel Sold in Six- and Seven-Figure Auction Deals Pulled Over Suspected AI Use
items.excerpt: A crime novel hailed as 'genius' that had secured six- and seven-figure US and UK publishing deals at auction was withdrawn by its agent after allegations the manuscript was AI-generated. A concrete case of AI detection reshaping acquisitions, author vetting and trust in the submission/auction pipeline. (The Bookseller is paywalled; date confirmed via article metadata, RECOVERY-pass via Googlebot RSS + WebFetch.)

items.title: ‘Clarity of Thought and Responsibility’: Can the Pope Move the Needle on AI Regulation?
items.excerpt: Reading Pope Leo XIV's AI encyclical (itself now published as a Melville House trade paperback), Publishing Perspectives draws out seven takeaways for the book trade on data ownership, creative-sector copyright, the Anthropic $1.5B settlement and workplace transformation — framing how publishers and authors should engage AI regulation. (Date from RSS pubDate, RECOVERY pass.)
